roadmap.goal: Since server v26.8.31.7 (commit 8c0b99756) GET /v1/deliveries/portfolio/{id} answers {active, archived}; the clients still read it as an array, so readable `lh delivery list` falls back to the generic key/value dump and the MCP lighthouse_delivery_list drops its summary. Fix: the client returns {active, archived} (an older server's array becomes {active: array, archived: []}, any other shape is an error); the CLI readable view shows the active Deliveries as today plus an Archived section; the MCP summary counts the active Deliveries; the integration smoke reads .active and also runs BEFORE a release (locally packed packages, against lighthouse:latest and :dev-latest, on every main push and nightly), gating the Release environment. Every step ends with `pnpm run ci` exit 0 in lighthouse-clients.
roadmap.paradigm_note: TypeScript / Vitest in lighthouse-clients; the clients keep their pure-reader / injected-client factory style. No fast-check dependency: finite domains are it.each tables. There is no DISTILL wave for a bugfix: RED is a crafter-authored regression test through the driving port (the client's request path against a fake fetch, `lh` against the fake Lighthouse in test-support, the MCP tool handler), which must fail on today's code for the bug's reason before production code changes.

scripts/smoke-integration.sh ghcr.io/letpeoplework/lighthouse:dev-latest with locally packed client+cli from HEAD -> exits 0
criteria: scripts/smoke-integration.sh <lighthouse-image> holds the body of today's smoke-integration job (ci.yml ~334-478): it starts the image, seeds the demo scenario, and runs every existing check against whatever `lh` (and MCP binary, if the smoke uses one) is on PATH. Behaviour is the same as today's job apart from the delivery check. It cleans up its container on exit (trap).

The delivery wait reads `any(.active[]; (.features | length) > 0)`; the readable check `expect_pretty "Delivery Date"` stays. No archived-section check in the smoke (the demo data seeds no archived Delivery; unit tests cover it).
RED/GREEN demonstrated locally with Docker as listed in red_to_green_tests; outputs (tail) captured in the report.
The post-publish smoke-integration job keeps `needs: release`, installs from npm as today, and runs the shared script against lighthouse:latest.

A new job runs before the release: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, pnpm build, pnpm pack of the packages into $RUNNER_TEMP, then installs the client and cli tarballs TOGETHER into one prefix (so the cli's pinned client dependency resolves to the packed client, not npm) and puts that prefix's bin on PATH; it runs the shared script in a matrix over ghcr.io/letpeoplework/lighthouse:latest and :dev-latest.
Triggers: the workflow gains `schedule` (nightly, a minute that is not :00 or :30) and `workflow_dispatch`; the pre-release job runs on main pushes, the schedule and dispatch.

The Release-gate job(s) (`unpublished` / `release`) list the pre-release job in `needs:` and only run for `github.event_name == 'push'`, so a nightly or manual run never requests the Release environment.
actionlint is clean on ci.yml; `pnpm run ci` exits 0.

docs/release-model.md (and docs/deployment.md if it describes the pipeline) say in plain words that the integration smoke now runs before the Release gate against the released and the next server image, and still runs after publish.

The two matrix legs can legitimately disagree: dev-latest may carry server changes not released yet. So the matrix sets fail-fast: false and each leg is named by its image; the latest leg gates the Release environment; the dev-latest leg runs and shows red when it fails (job summary / annotation naming the image) but does NOT block the release (e.g. continue-on-error on that leg, or the release needs only the latest leg). The nightly run against dev-latest is the early warning for unreleased server API changes.
